evidence_items.publisher: The New York Times Company (complaint, S.D.N.Y. 1:23-cv-11195)

receipt.public_excerpt:
Between the Common Crawl, WebText, and WebText2 datasets, the

Defendants likely used millions of Times-owned works in full in order to train the GPT models.

evidence_items.explanation: The complaint uses public dataset analysis to tie millions of Times works to the datasets used to train OpenAI's GPT models. This supports the 'other models trained on a great deal of its content' part, though the wording is 'likely'.

evidence_items.publisher: The New York Times Company (complaint, S.D.N.Y. 1:23-cv-11195)

receipt.public_excerpt:
Exhibit J provides scores of additional examples of memorization of Times Works

by GPT-4. Upon information and belief, these examples represent a small fraction of Times Works

evidence_items.explanation: GPT-4 reproducing Times articles verbatim is direct evidence that it was exposed to that content. But the claim that this is a large share of Times works is pleaded 'upon information and belief', not shown.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4, 'The New York Times is not telling the full story', paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: like any single source, their content didn’t meaningfully contribute to the training of our existing models

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI publicly disputed that Times content was a significant part of training. This shows the 'great deal' point was contested and not proven when the post was published. It is a self-interested party statement, and it does not deny that Times content was used.

evidence_items.locator: Section 3, 'Regurgitation is a rare bug', paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: it’s more common when particular content appears more than once in training data, like if pieces of it appear on lots of different public websites.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI offers another explanation for GPT-4's verbatim output: copies of Times text on other sites. This weakens the inference that memorization proves large-scale direct training on Times content.

unresolved_gaps: OpenAI has not publicly disclosed GPT-4's training data, so the volume of Times content in it is not public.
No court had made factual findings on training by the evaluation date. Summary judgment was still pending in October 2026, per secondary trackers.
Discovery material on training data is largely sealed.
